# Conformance summary: after Job 1 (talent-free comparison)

Generated by hand against the nine goldens regenerated by
`FOREVER_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test --tags=with_db ./sim/conformance/...`
on top of `sim/conformance`'s talent-free rework (every preset now
builds with an empty talent string; talent-only abilities moved to each
golden's own "Talent-gated spells" section). All counts below are at
level 60, the level every preset reaches, so a spell that is only
registered below 60 is not represented in these totals (see each
golden's own full level ladder - 10/20/30/38/40/50/60 - for those).

"Before" is the committed golden on `forever` before this rework (full
real talent builds); "after" is the new golden's two sections. Compare
with care: "before" buried every talent-modifier row as a mismatch
(Frostbolt/Earth Shock/Starfire's talent-reduced cost, Wrath's
talent-reduced cast time, etc.), so a drop in mismatch count from before
to after is mostly that burial being removed, not fixes landing. The
real engine defects are the "after" mismatch tables below.

Shaman's huge mismatch count is almost entirely one systemic cause
(every totem's GCD and duration, see below), not 246 independent
defects - see the shaman section's lead note.

## Likely-cause vocabulary

Every mismatch below is tagged with one of:

- **stale vanilla literal** - the engine still carries an old
  pre-Forever Classic number (cost, cast time, cooldown, or dot
  duration) that Forever's spellconst build changed and the engine's
  source was never updated to match.
- **missing aura duration** - the client names a nonzero duration but
  the engine's spell has neither a `RelatedSelfBuff` nor a `Dot` on the
  current target for `compare.go`'s `engineDuration` to read (see its
  doc comment), so it reports 0 even if the ability's real effect
  duration is implemented some other way (a target debuff that isn't a
  Dot, a trap's armed lifetime versus its burn tick length, etc.) -
  this tag means "not visible to this report," not necessarily "not
  implemented at all."
- **percent-of-mana cost vs. flat client column** - the engine spends
  `ManaCostOptions.BaseCost` as a fraction of base mana (Classic's
  original cost model for pet summons, shapeshifts, and a few hybrid
  abilities), while the client's spellconst `cost` column reads a flat
  0 for the same spell. This may be a genuine stale formula, or it may
  be that Forever's client stores a percent-cost spell's real cost in a
  field this report does not read yet and 0 is expected - flagged, not
  confirmed, pending a look at the client's own percent-cost field.
- **registration gap** - the spell's own `SpellConfig` simply never
  sets the field in question (no `RequiredLevel`, no `Cost`, no `CD`),
  so the engine's default zero-value is read as a mismatch rather than
  a missing number.
- **semantic mismatch** - both sides have a real, correct number, but
  they are not measuring the same thing (a trap's total armed lifetime
  versus its damage-tick length).
- **not a real spell** - the client's class table carries an entry
  (like the generic melee "Attack" button) that was never meant to be
  an engine-registered spell at all.

## Required-level mismatches (registration gaps, not numbers)

Every row here is the engine reporting `RequiredLevel = 0` for a spell
the client's `spell_level` places above 1, i.e. the spell's own
`SpellConfig` never sets `RequiredLevel`. One exception is called out
separately. This is a work list, not a numeric target - the fix in
every row is "add `RequiredLevel: <client value>` to this spell's
config," not "change a number."

**Exception - a real numeric mismatch, not a registration gap:** Paladin
**Holy Shield** rank 1, in the talent-gated section, reports client 40
vs. engine 30 - both sides set a real required level, they just
disagree by 10. Likely cause: stale vanilla literal (Holy Shield was
learnable at 30 in original Classic; Forever's client moved it to 40
and the engine's rank table was not updated).

### Shaman

Shaman's count is dominated by one systemic pair of defects repeated
across every totem (Strength of Earth, Grace of Air, Windfury, Windwall,
Stoneskin, Mana Spring, Healing Stream, Magma, Searing, Tremor):

| Spell | Field | Client | Engine | Likely cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Every totem (all ranks) | gcd_ms | 1000 | 1500 | stale vanilla literal - the engine still gives every totem the standard 1.5s GCD; Forever's client gives totems a 1s GCD and the engine was never updated for this class of spell |
| Every totem (all ranks) | duration_ms | 300000 | 0 | missing aura duration (a totem's lifetime is a self-buff this report's `engineDuration` is not finding - likely stored on the totem unit rather than the caster, which `RelatedSelfBuff`/`Dot(target)` do not reach) |
| Attack | cast_time_ms, required_level | 2200 / 10-60 | 0 / 0 | not a real spell - this is the client's generic melee "Attack" button entry; it should not be matched against any engine spell at all, and the client-class JSON comparison should likely exclude or special-case it |
| Lightning Bolt ranks 4-10 | cost, cast_time_ms | 60.00-220.00 / 2500 | 75.00-265.00 / 3000 | stale vanilla literal - ranks 1-3 already match; ranks 4+ are still on the old Classic cast time (3000ms) and cost table instead of Forever's (2500ms) |
| Chain Lightning (all ranks) | cost, cast_time_ms | 225.00-485.00 / 2000 | 280.00-605.00 / 2500 | stale vanilla literal, same shape as Lightning Bolt |
| Stormstrike (talent-gated) | cost, cooldown_ms | 125.00 / 8000 | 319.20 / 20000 | cost is percent-of-mana vs. flat client column (`BaseCost: .21`); cooldown is a stale vanilla literal (20s was live Classic's cooldown; Forever's client shortened it to 8s) |
| Earth Shock, Frost Shock (all ranks) | duration_ms | 2000 / 8000 | 0 | missing aura duration |
| Water Shield (talent-gated) | cooldown_ms | 15000 | 0 | registration gap - no `CD` configured |
| Rage of the Farseer (talent-gated) | gcd_ms | 0 | 1500 | registration gap - a cooldown-only talent ability the client flags GCD-less, same shape as Warlock's Bane of Havoc |

### Rogue

| Spell | Field | Client | Engine | Likely cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stealth | cooldown_ms | 10000 | 0 | registration gap - no `CD` configured |
| Adrenaline Rush, Blade Flurry, Expose Armor, Ghostly Strike, Hemorrhage, Premeditation, Riposte, Rupture, Slice and Dice | duration_ms | 6000-30000 | 0 | missing aura duration |

Rogue has the fewest matches of any class (0 in the main table at level
60, 3 in the talent-gated table) but also the fewest distinct defects -
every rogue mismatch is one of two systemic causes (missing aura
duration and Stealth's missing cooldown), not 28 independent numeric
bugs. CombatSwordsRogue's pre-existing WeaponExpertise talent-rewrite
panic (sim/rogue/talents.go, tracked separately) does not affect this
report: it only panicked under that preset's real 5-point talent spend,
and the empty-talent comparison build never reaches that code path.

## Open question worth a follow-up lane

Every "percent-of-mana cost vs. flat client column" row above (Hunter's
Bestial Wrath and Multi-Shot, Warlock's four summons, Druid's Cat
Form/Moonkin Form/Innervate, Shaman's Stormstrike) should be checked
against the client's own build data for a percent-cost field before
being treated as engine bugs - if Forever's spellconst genuinely has no
percent-cost column, these may all be correct engine behavior that this
report simply cannot verify, and the real work item is extending
`sim/core/spellconst` and this report's `rowFor`, not the spell code.
